## Priority call
The binding constraint is DAY18 inventory, and the biggest controllable leak is mobile PDP/checkout friction. I would run three priorities in this order, with one owner for the inventory guardrail, one designer/developer block for PDP work, and one Klaviyo/post-purchase test.

### Diagnosis in numbers
- Shopify current vs prior: sessions 20,000→25,000 (+25%), orders 600→500 (-16.7%), net product revenue $54,000→$45,000 (-16.7%), AOV flat at $90 ($54,000/600, $45,000/500).
- Mobile is the break: mobile sessions 15,000→20,000, mobile orders 400→300, so mobile CVR 2.67%→1.5%. Desktop CVR is flat at 4.0% (200/5,000).
- Funnel: ATC rate 10%→8% (2,000/20,000 vs 2,000/25,000); ATC→checkout 60%→50% (1,200/2,000 vs 1,000/2,000); checkout→order 50% both (600/1,200 vs 500/1,000).
- Meta: CPM $12→$15, CTR 1.5%→1.2%, estimated clicks 22,500→17,600, CPC $0.80→$1.25. Reported ROAS looks fine (3.0→3.2), but Meta reported $70,400 + Klaviyo $14,000 = $84,400 against $45,000 Shopify revenue. That is overlap, not incremental truth. Use Shopify as source of truth.
- DAY18 stock: 210 units / 8 per day = 26.25 days cover. Replenishment is 500 units in 35 days. Demand over 35 days = 280; gap = 70 units. To avoid a stockout before arrival, sell no more than 210/35 = 6 DAY18/day. That is a 25% reduction from current pace. Replenishment cash = 500 × $28 = $14,000, protected by policy.

### Priority 1 — Inventory-aware acquisition reallocation (owner/ops + paid media)
Set a hard DAY18 sell-through cap of 6/day until the replenishment lands. If current 8/day continues, stockout is about day 26, leaving roughly 9 days uncovered. Do not buy extra inventory. Shift the $3,000 test budget away from broad DAY18 prospecting and mature “Desk-to-trail” creative (55% of spend) toward accessories and educational creative that supports conversion: laptop-fit education and “water-resistant, not waterproof.” Use no new discount; none is approved. Metrics: DAY18 days cover, units/day, accessory units, contribution after ad spend, and cash reserved for the $14,000 replenishment. Lever: acquire more customers, but only where inventory can support it.

### Priority 2 — Fix mobile PDP and checkout friction (conversion)
The support tickets say the PDP is not answering buyer questions: 42 delivery-date questions, 28 15-inch-laptop questions, 18 waterproof questions in 30 days. The page puts laptop sizing and delivery below reviews, and the CTA says “Buy now.” Move sizing, delivery window, and water-resistance language above reviews. Say plainly: “Water-resistant fabric, not waterproof.” For laptops, do not claim 15-inch fit unless it is verified; current fact is a padded 13-inch sleeve. Publish measured sleeve dimensions once ops supplies them. Change CTA to “Add to cart” and show the 4–7 business-day estimate near the button. Add an Added-to-Cart flow; Klaviyo currently has checkout abandonment only, at 24 hours.

Arithmetic: restoring ATC→checkout from 50% to the prior 60% gives 1,200 starts; at 50% checkout completion that is 600 orders vs 500, or +100 orders ≈ +$9,000 at $90 AOV. Recovering half the mobile CVR gap gives 20,000 × (2.67%−1.5%)/2 ≈ +117 mobile orders ≈ +$10,530. Do not add these together; they overlap. Apply only with the DAY18 cap or an accessory mix.

### Priority 3 — Retention/cash via post-purchase accessory cross-sell (retention + CX)
The 90-day repeat rate is 14%, and 72% of current customers are new. Klaviyo has 12,000 marketable profiles but only welcome and checkout abandonment flows, with no holdout. Build a post-purchase flow for DAY18 buyers: set delivery expectations, explain the 13-inch sleeve, and cross-sell the cable pouch ($20) and steel bottle ($32). This increases purchases per customer without consuming DAY18 stock. Full-price only; no discount approval. Also add proactive delivery-status messaging to reduce the 42 delivery-date tickets. Metrics: repeat-purchase rate, accessory attach rate, AOV, contribution after message costs, and delivery tickets. Do not judge success by opens or clicks; the reported 52% open, 1.1% click, 0.18% order rates are platform metrics, not profit.

### What I would defer
Do not run a broad DAY18 acquisition push, do not claim waterproof or 15-inch fit, do not launch a sitewide discount, and do not buy more inventory. Two weeks is enough to cap stock, fix the mobile PDP, add an ATC flow, and test accessory cross-sell. If DAY18 stock can be accelerated or partly reallocated, Priority 2 can be expanded; otherwise inventory gates it.
questions: What is the measured internal laptop sleeve dimension or opening for DAY18, and is 15-inch fit actually verified? This determines whether we can answer the 28 laptop-fit tickets and what creative can legally claim.
What are current sell-through, days cover, and replenishment lead times for POUCH and BOTTLE? This determines whether we can profitably shift demand from DAY18 to accessories.

Can the 500-unit DAY18 replenishment be split or accelerated, or can we open a transparent waitlist/pre-order to cover the projected 9-day gap? If not, the 6/day cap is the only inventory-safe option.
assumptions: DAY18 daily units sold of 8 is net of returns and continues absent intervention; no seasonality adjustment was supplied.
The 500-unit replenishment arrives in 35 days with no partial earlier receipt, and no additional inventory purchase is approved.
The stated pick/pack and merchant shipping costs apply as given; accessory contribution excludes allocated shipping if added to an existing order.
No discounts without owner approval, and no waterproof, 15-inch-fit, medical, sustainability, or lifetime-durability claims are supported.
Meta and Klaviyo reported revenue are not reconciled to Shopify and should not be treated as incremental.
Support themes and ticket counts are directional evidence, not verbatim testimonials or controlled test results.
POUCH and BOTTLE stock can be sold as add-ons/cross-sells, but their current sell-through and replenishment status are not supplied.
